lead.title: Meta built a humanoid prototype called Max with Fourier Intelligence in three months
lead.summary: The Information reports Meta worked with Shanghai-based Fourier to assemble a roughly 1.5 m, 48 kg humanoid codenamed Max in about three months, running on NVIDIA Jetson Thor compute with five-fingered hands and an expressive face display. Work on a Max 2 is already underway, and Meta says the effort is internal research with no plans to sell the units.

top_stories.title: LeCun's Llama-4 postmortem: rushed timelines, lost team, and the case for world models
top_stories.summary: Yann LeCun published a detailed retrospective on the Llama lineage, saying he championed open-sourcing Llama-2 but attributes Llama-4's weak reception to rushed product pressure and the dispersal of the original FAIR Paris team. In a companion thread he contrasts LLM declarative knowledge with JEPA-style world models that need far less data.

top_stories.title: A 109M-parameter JEPA-style trainer rivals 72B LLMs on representation alignment
top_stories.summary: A new paper by Randall Balestriero and Yann LeCun, promoted by LeCun himself, proves a version of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: with anti-collapse regularizers, the similarity structure of training data determines learned representations. A 109M text encoder trained this way aligns with DINOv2/CLIP better than every evaluated LM up to 72B, using about 42x fewer examples than next-token prediction.

items.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
items.summary: Shows the staged lifecycle (pretraining, midtraining, SFT, RL) is not algorithmically fundamental: RL objectives can be derived as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, unifying all stages under one likelihood-based trainer while improving the accuracy-compute tradeoff.

items.title: Apple trains UI navigation agents with online RL on live iOS apps
items.summary: An 8B RL agent trained across hundreds of concurrent virtual iOS devices with a planning-plus-grounding setup improves out-of-distribution Android generalization nearly 7x over the SFT baseline and outperforms Gemini-3.5-Flash on real applications.

items.title: AB-Attention accelerates video diffusion transformers without retraining
items.summary: A training-free block-sparse attention method skips 89-92% of attention on Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo while improving PSNR by up to 4.4 dB over the strongest baseline and delivering up to 2.23x end-to-end speedup.

items.title: EditAgent rethinks agentic image editing
items.summary: A study finds general-purpose agentic editors produce no usable result in over 40% of expert-annotated cases; EditAgent routes steps across general and specialized editors with per-candidate verification, preferred by experts in 78.5% of decided comparisons.

items.title: Unlocking any-order generation in pretrained autoregressive image models
items.summary: A recipe adapts raster-scan AR image models into any-order generators at 13-33% extra compute, beating MaskGIT on ImageNet inpainting (FID 6.21 vs 10.44) while keeping the standard AR inference stack intact.

items.title: HackerBooks: HackerTube, but for books mentioned on Hacker News
items.summary: A companion site to Karpathy's HackerTube indexes and surfaces books referenced across Hacker News discussions, hitting 651 points within hours of launch.

items.title: OmniDiff: a content-aware Git difftool in Rust
items.summary: An open-source, super-fast Git difftool that understands content structure rather than plain line diffs, trending on Hacker News.

items.title: Memdoor: five Qwen3.8-27B models beat Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard
items.summary: An open-source multi-agent workflow shows five cooperating Qwen3.8-27B models outscoring a frontier model on LiveCodeBench Hard; it drew 409 points and 200 comments on Hacker News.

items.title: Confetti: build hardware gadgets using plain English
items.summary: A new tool for designing and prototyping hardware gadgets described in natural language, bridging plain English and electronics prototyping.
